Chapter One: Rethinking What It Means to Follow Jesus in a Comfortable World
Let's be honest—it's so easy to fall into routines that feel safe and familiar, isn't it? Most of us wake up, head to work, take care of our families, and do our best to do the right thing. In all of this, faith can start to feel like just another item on the to-do list. Maybe it's a Sunday morning habit, or a set of beliefs that just kind of fit in with everything else.
But sometimes, there's this quiet restlessness that sneaks in. You know that feeling when something seems off, like maybe the faith we're living doesn't quite line up with the stories of Jesus and his first followers?
That tension can show up in the most unexpected moments. Picture a group of friends, curled up in a living room, sharing their hopes and worries. Someone, worn out from a long week, wonders out loud, "Is there more to faith than just being good and showing up at church?" Another friend, who's been reading about Christians in other countries, tells stories about people risking everything for what they believe. The question just hangs in the air: What if following Jesus actually means giving up comfort, security—even those dreams we've worked so hard to build?
For a lot of us, the idea of radical faith can feel pretty far away. The world around us celebrates achievement, independence, and chasing happiness. Success is often measured by what you can earn, own, or experience. Even in church, it's common to hear how faith can make life better—how it brings peace, purpose, maybe even prosperity.
But then, you look at what Jesus actually taught, and it seems like he's pointing us in a different direction. He called people to walk away from their possessions, to love their enemies, to take care of the poor, and to put God above everything else.
It's not that comfort or success are bad. The real problem comes when those things become the main goal—when they start shaping what our faith looks like. Over time, it's all too easy to build a version of Christianity that slips neatly into the American Dream. A faith that asks little, costs little, and doesn't really push us to change.
But if you read the stories of Jesus with fresh eyes, his call is anything but safe or easy.
There's this one story that sticks with me—a young professional who seemed to have it all. Great job, nice apartment, busy social life. But even with all that, there was this sense of emptiness that wouldn't go away. After hearing about people who'd given up big careers to serve in tough places, she started to wonder what it actually means to follow Jesus. Is faith just about being good and enjoying blessings, or is there something deeper?
These kinds of questions can be uncomfortable, but they're important. Most of us don't notice how easily faith gets shaped by our culture, or how quickly we soften the teachings of Jesus to fit what feels convenient. The stories of the early church—full of sacrifice and boldness—stand in sharp contrast to the easy, comfortable faith that's so common today.
So, here's an invitation: take a moment and really reflect. What if the version of Christianity that's most familiar isn't the one Jesus actually meant for us? What if real faith means letting go of comfort, security, and even some of those dreams we've held onto?
This journey starts with honest questions and a willingness to see faith in a whole new light.
